label: Person
name: Addai Scher
summary:
Addai Scher (1867–1915) was a Chaldean Catholic bishop and Orientalist scholar who served as Archbishop of Siirt (Seert) in southeastern Turkey and was martyred by Ottoman forces during the Armenian Genocide and associated massacres of Christian minorities. Born into a Chaldean Catholic family in Khanaqin, he pursued advanced studies in European Orientalism and became one of the most important scholars of Syriac Christianity in the early twentieth century.

Scher's scholarly work was extraordinary in breadth and importance. He was a prolific researcher of Syriac manuscripts, producing critical editions, catalogues, and studies of Syriac Christian literature that remained standard references for decades. His 'Histoire nestorienne' — a critical edition and translation of the Chronicle of Seert — made an important source for early Eastern Christian history accessible to modern scholarship. He also compiled catalogues of Syriac manuscripts in European and Middle Eastern libraries.

On 20 June 1915, Scher was murdered by Ottoman irregular forces during the massacres that targeted the Christian population of the Hakkari-Tur Abdin region alongside the Armenian Genocide. His death was part of the systematic elimination of the Christian minority populations of eastern Anatolia. He was beatified by Pope Francis in 2015 — exactly a century after his death — as one of the martyrs of the Armenian Genocide's Christian victims.
